biggest_catch: The $795 annual fee is the whole story. Year-one math: 100,000 Ultimate Rewards points are worth at least $1,000 as cash back, so $1,000 bonus value minus the $795 fee leaves roughly $205 net in the first year, before counting the card's travel credits (Chase advertises up to $2,000 in annual travel credits). Only claim this if you were already going to spend $6,000 in 3 months on normal purchases and you will actually use the credits; never spend extra to hit the target. Same restrictions as Preferred apply: the unpublished 5/24 pattern, and no new Sapphire bonus if you earned one in the past 48 months or currently hold a Sapphire card.
catches: Only claim this if you were already going to spend the money anyway; never spend extra just to hit the $6,000 minimum, because manufactured spending turns a bonus into debt.

Year-one math: the 100,000-point bonus is worth at least $1,000 as cash back, minus the $795 annual fee, which leaves about $205 net before travel credits. Chase advertises up to $2,000 in annual travel credits, but credits only have value if you actually use them. From year two the $795 fee applies without a bonus, so keep the card only if your real spending plus real credit usage beats $795 a year.

Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which typically knocks a few points off your credit score for a short time. Chase also uses its unpublished 5/24 pattern: applicants with five or more newly opened personal cards across any issuer in the last 24 months are generally denied.
This card's APR is around 20% or higher, so carrying a balance would wipe out the bonus fast. Pay the statement balance in full every month or this offer loses you money.
Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern: five or more new personal cards opened in the last 24 months generally means denial, even with excellent credit. This is not published in Chase's official terms.
A new Sapphire bonus is not available if you received a Sapphire bonus in the past 48 months or currently hold a Sapphire card. Check the current application terms if you are inside that window.
The account must be open and not in default when the bonus is paid, and the bonus is paid only once per account.

steps: Go to the official Chase travel cards page, select Sapphire Reserve, and read the current offer headline and the Pricing & Terms before anything else.
Confirm your eligibility: you have not received a Sapphire new-cardmember bonus in the last 48 months and do not currently hold a Sapphire card.
Apply online. Expect a hard credit inquiry.
Use the card for the purchases you were already planning, totaling at least $6,000 in the first 3 months from account opening.
Pay the statement balance in full every month; do not carry a balance at the ~20%+ APR.
Allow 6-8 weeks after the spending requirement is met for the 100,000 points to post, and confirm they appear in your Ultimate Rewards account.
Before the second $795 annual fee hits, audit which travel credits you actually used and decide whether to keep, downgrade, or cancel based on real use.
timing: Spend $6,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Bonus posts after qualifying purchases, typically 6-8 weeks after the spending requirement is met.
